name: CELLTREAT 229101 1 well
author: Ramona Optics
notes: CELLTREAT 1 Well Tissue Culture Plate with Lid, part number 229101 (Fisher Scientific catalog number 50-114-9068): one rectangular flat-bottom well filling a standard microplate footprint. Clear polystyrene, tissue culture treated, sterile, non-pyrogenic, RNase/DNase free, individually packed, 50 per case. NO DRAWING IS PUBLISHED: CELLTREAT's product page (web_reference) gives no dimensions beyond a cell growth area of 97.4 cm^2, the statement that the plate 'has the same footprint as standard multiple well plates', and that it takes an 11.4 x 7.3 cm (4.5 x 2.875 in) nylon membrane. Everything dimensional below is therefore DERIVED or ASSUMED and has NOT been checked against a drawing or a physical plate; measure a plate before relying on it. Units in meters. FOOTPRINT, assumed: the ANSI/SLAS 1-2004 footprint, 127.76 x 85.48 mm, from the maker's 'same footprint' statement. Distributors list the plate with roughly rounded sizes that agree with it: 12.8 x 8.57 cm (Amazon), 5.05 x 3.39 in (JangoCell), 5-1/16 x 3-3/8 in (Global Industrial). HEIGHT, from distributors: 0.57 in = 14.5 mm (JangoCell) and 9/16 in = 14.3 mm (Global Industrial); 14.5 mm is recorded. Amazon lists 1.54 cm, taken here to be the height with the lid on and not recorded. WELL, derived: the well is taken as a rectangle the same distance inside the footprint on all four sides whose area is the published 97.4 cm^2 growth area: (127.76 - 2m) x (85.48 - 2m) = 9740 mm^2 gives m = 2.84 mm, a well floor 122.1 mm along the plate's length ('width') by 79.8 mm along its width ('height'), 97.4 cm^2. The real well has rounded corners, which this ignores, so the true sides are slightly longer than recorded. It is consistent with the 114 x 73 mm membrane the maker says fits. 'diameter' is the shorter side, 79.8 mm, for readers that do not know the rectangle keys. DEPTH, assumed: 12.5 mm, the 14.5 mm height less a floor taken to be 2 mm above the plane the plate rests on; no thickness, elevation or working volume is published, so those keys are left out. The well is centered on the plate (A1 is the plate's center). pitch is the plate's width: one well has no neighbor to be spaced from, and this keeps the lattice's one cell on the plate and wider than 'diameter' for readers that fall back to it. Use 'pitch' and origin reference to compute all well centers.
